title: Assam chief secretary holds review after Guwahati cloudburst-like rainfall
summary: Heavy rainfall leads to widespread waterlogging and disruption of normal life in Assam.
full_content:
The heavy downpour led to widespread waterlogging, disruption of normal life, and considerable inconvenience to the public. Notably, this rainfall intensity exceeded the 120 mm recorded over 24 hours on 31 May 2025.
The India Meteorological Department, Assam State Disaster Management Authority, and District Disaster Management Authority have been directed to issue timely and advance weather forecasts and advisories. These measures aim to enable residents to take necessary precautions and plan their movement, supported by advance traffic advisories from the city police.
The National Highways Authority of India has been instructed to ensure that concessionaires remain available round-the-clock for clearing cross-drainage culverts, operating pumps, and removing silt deposits following waterlogging. Key stretches identified include Tetelia–Jalukbari, Excel Care–Gorchuk, Koinadhara–Tripura Road, and Jorabat–Khanapara.
The Guwahati Municipal Corporation, Guwahati Metropolitan Development Authority, and the Water Resources Department have been directed to maintain 24×7 operational readiness to address waterlogging in Anil Nagar, Navin Nagar, Lachit Nagar, Rukmini Nagar and other vulnerable areas.
The Public Works Department (Roads) has been tasked with ensuring thorough desiltation of drains and preventing recurrence of waterlogging, particularly in areas such as GS Road near Bhangagarh. Strict directions have been issued for immediate, time-bound dredging, desiltation, and cleaning of all drainage channels. Any lapses in preparedness, maintenance, or response will invite accountability.
In connection with the Maligaon incident involving the loss of a life, the District Commissioner has been directed to institute a magisterial enquiry to determine responsibility. Incidents resulting in loss of life due to preventable causes are unacceptable and will be dealt with firmly.
Given the likelihood of continued heavy rainfall this season, residents in landslide-prone hilly areas are being alerted to remain vigilant and take necessary precautions to avoid loss of life and property.
All departments and agencies are operating round-the-clock in close coordination to address waterlogging, expedite drainage, and restore normalcy. The situation has improved in several areas, while targeted interventions are ongoing in the remaining affected locations.
Notably, waterlogging near Jorabat was cleared expeditiously due to prior dredging and drainage improvements towards Byrnihat, underscoring the importance of sustained desiltation efforts.
In view of past incidents, including landslides last year, the District Administration has been directed to maintain heightened vigilance in vulnerable areas and ensure coordinated response, mitigation, and relief measures.
As per the forecast by the India Meteorological Department, occasional rain and thunderstorms are likely over the coming days. All agencies have been directed to remain on high alert.

title: Flash floods kill woman in Guwahati; city paralysed by heavy rains
summary: Flash floods kill woman in Guwahati due to heavy rains, severely disrupting life.
full_content:
Flash floods kill woman in Guwahati; city paralysed by heavy rains
A woman lost her life as flash floods and severe waterlogging wreaked havoc across Guwahati following incessant rainfall since Sunday night, severely disrupting normal life across the city.
The deceased has been identified as Payal Nath, a woman in her 30s from Dharapur. She reportedly slipped into an open roadside drain in the Maligaon Chariali area around 9:30 pm on Sunday while navigating waterlogged streets. Swept away by strong currents, her body was recovered by SDRF personnel early Monday, nearly 100 metres from the spot. She was taken to Pandu FRU, where doctors declared her brought dead.
There is a report of landslide at Kamakhya Hills on Sunday night, but there was no casualty.
Relentless downpour triggered flash floods and widespread inundation, bringing the city to a standstill. Several low-lying areas, including Hatigaon, Anil Nagar, Beltola, Survey, Lokhra, Sijubari, Nabin Nagar and Rajgarh Link Road, were among the worst affected. Water entered homes, while knee-deep flooding turned streets into virtual lakes overnight.
Road connectivity was severely hit as key stretches went under water, leading to massive traffic congestion, particularly in Lokhra and adjoining areas. Commuters were stranded on roads and flyovers, with many forced to wade through floodwaters to reach their destinations. The situation continued well into Monday morning, crippling movement in major parts of the city.
The city recorded 125.5 mm of rainfall on Sunday night.
According to the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), waterlogging was reported in several locations across Kamrup Metro district, including Rukminigaon, Ghoramara, Juripar, Panjabari, Hatigaon, Sijubari, Satgaon, Jatia, Sawkuchi, Anil Nagar, Nabin Nagar, Rajgarh, Sorumotoria, Bormotoria, Narengi, Maligaon and Boragaon.
Emergency helplines were activated, and rescue teams along with boats were deployed by Fire and Emergency Services and SDRF following distress calls. Around 50 people have been evacuated from affected areas so far.
Authorities said the water level has started receding in some parts. As many as 22 major pumps and 35 portable pumps have been pressed into service in areas such as Rukminigaon, Tarun Nagar, Anil Nagar, Lachit Nagar and Bharalu Mukh to drain out accumulated water.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) had earlier forecast moderate to heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds across Assam and Meghalaya between April 17 and 19. It had also warned of isolated heavy to very heavy rainfall. Data released on April 19 confirmed very heavy rainfall ranging between 12 and 20 cm at isolated places across Assam.
In view of the situation, the Kamrup Metropolitan district administration ordered closure of all educational institutions, both government and private, under the Guwahati Municipal Corporation area on Monday.
Residents expressed frustration over recurring flooding. A resident of Nabin Nagar said the area gets submerged even after brief spells of rain, forcing people to remain stranded for hours.
Authorities continue to monitor the situation in low-lying areas and have urged citizens to remain cautious.
